# Physical cooling-channel construction

`build_channel_construction(circuit, centerline)` builds lazy section geometry
for CAD and the native 3D viewer. It evaluates the circuit's original geometry
and design-input context, then creates drawing dimensions separately. It does
not change the simulation height, pitch, rib width, coolant area, hydraulic
diameter, heat-transfer perimeters, or coolant centerline.

## Main walls and liners

`Wall` accepts `role="main"` (the default) or `role="liner"`:

```python
tube_wall = psf.regen.Wall(material=copper, thickness=0.6e-3)
liner = psf.regen.Wall(material=silver, thickness=insert_thickness, role="liner")
# Pass walls=[liner, tube_wall] to CoolingCircuit.
```

List layers from hot gas to coolant, with all liners before the main walls.
A circuit requires at least one main wall. Every main layer contributes to
the channel-wall thickness; for rounded channels these are the layers forming
the tubes and the material between neighboring coolant passages. A liner lies
only on the combustion side and does not add to the tube-wall thickness.
All layers still participate in through-wall thermal conduction.

`circuit.channel_wall_thickness(x)` and design input `t_wall` sum the main
layers. `circuit.hot_side_layer_thickness(x)` and `t_hot_layer` sum the liners.
`circuit.total_thickness(x)` and `t_wall_total` include both, describing the
complete stack between hot gas and coolant. The wall-layer plot includes all
layers on the hot side and assumes a closeout made from the main layers only.

Names and list positions do not assign roles. Existing calls and saved `Wall`
objects without a role default to main walls; explicitly mark existing liners
and regenerate saved simulations. The RL10 silver throat insert uses
`role="liner"`, while its stainless steel tube wall uses the main default.

## Rib heat transfer

Set `enable_fin` and `rib_material` on each `CoolingCircuit` independently:

```python
circuit = psf.regen.CoolingCircuit(
    # ... other circuit inputs ...
    enable_fin=True,
    rib_material=psf.common.solids.GRCop42,
)
```

`enable_fin` defaults to `True`. Set it to `False` to omit the fin heat-transfer
enhancement while retaining the rib geometry. `rib_material` defaults to `None`,
which uses the coolant-facing main-wall material. An explicit material supplies
`get_k(T)` to the fin calculation only; wall conduction still uses the individual
wall-layer materials. For rounded tubes an override represents an effective fin
material, not an additional wall layer.

`ThrustChamber` no longer accepts `enable_fin` or overwrites circuit settings.
Move any previous chamber-level setting onto each relevant circuit. Saved
circuits retain their existing enabled/disabled setting and default to the
wall material if they predate the material override.

## Squared channels

Squared sections use planes perpendicular to the engine axis, for both
straight and helical channels. Each origin remains on the section-reference
centerline, and the first in-plane axis points radially outward. Consequently
the engine axis is at `(-r_ref, 0)` in local plane coordinates. The channel floor
and roof are exact circles about that point.

`build_axis_normal_section_planes(centerline)` provides these planes directly.
They are also available through `CoolingCircuit.section_planes(axis_normal=True)`
and `ResolvedChannel.axis_normal_section_planes`. The original flow-normal
`section_planes` interfaces retain their behavior.

Let `alpha = atan(dr_ref/dx)` be the signed meridional slope angle, using the
existing `alpha` convention, and let `gamma` be the helix angle measured from
the meridian. The physical drawing dimensions are

```text
height_transverse = h / cos(alpha)
pitch_transverse  = theta / cos(gamma_nominal)
```

Here `theta` is the simulation's local angular pitch, already reduced by
`cos(gamma_nominal)`. Construction uses the stored nominal helix law. If a
numerical layout changes a seed's angular path, its derivative changes the
local `gamma` used for rib projection; the nominal pitch allocation stays the
same. A geometry-only circuit without a stored helix law uses the derivatives
of its cylindrical centerline. Cylindrical derivatives avoid interpreting a
coarsely sampled helix chord as an inward radial slope.

The complete wall stack also needs the meridional projection. Because the
reference centerline already includes the hot-side liners, the radii are

```text
r_floor = r_ref - t_hot_layer + (t_hot_layer + t_wall) / cos(alpha)
r_roof  = r_floor + h / cos(alpha)
```

This applies the projection once to each wall layer.

## Rib projection

A simple wedge would produce a rib that thickens toward the roof. The
construction instead intersects the floor and roof circles with the two
projected faces of each rib.

There is also a shear when both the contour slope and helix are nonzero.
In a local radial/circumferential frame at a rib center, projection along the
coolant tangent onto an engine-axis-normal plane gives

```text
radial displacement from local height h:          h / cos(alpha)
circumferential displacement from local height h: h tan(alpha) tan(gamma)
circumferential displacement from local width w:  w / cos(gamma)
```

Thus define

```text
s = sin(alpha) tan(gamma)
d = rib_width / (2 cos(gamma))
```

and draw the two rib faces as parallel lines in the transverse plane:

```text
v - s (u - r_ref) = +d
v - s (u - r_ref) = -d
```

For a circle of radius `R`, substitute `u = R cos(delta)` and
`v = R sin(delta)`. Its intersections with those lines follow directly:

```text
delta = atan(s) + asin((-s r_ref +/- d) / (R sqrt(1 + s*s)))
```

Each channel's lower and upper boundaries use the inward-facing intersections
at the rib centers `-pitch_transverse/2` and `+pitch_transverse/2`. The two
circles then supply the floor and roof arcs, joined by straight rib faces.
Invalid intersections and a closed channel opening raise errors.

The local rib normal in `(axial, radial, circumferential)` coordinates is

```text
n_rib = (-sin(gamma) cos(alpha), -sin(gamma) sin(alpha), cos(gamma))
```

It has unit length. The two face offsets differ by exactly `rib_width` along
this normal at the floor, roof, and every intermediate point. At zero slope
the formula reduces to `half_pitch - asin(rib_width / (2 R cos(gamma)))`.
With zero helix it becomes the usual constant-width rib between annular
channels.

These are local tangent-plane projections: `alpha` and `gamma` are held
constant across a station's section. They preserve the requested rib thickness
in that local model. They do not calculate a globally exact normal offset of
a curved helicoidal surface; curvature, changes of helix angle through the
channel height, and loft interpolation introduce differences between the
local model and the resulting solid. The station spacing controls the axial
loft approximation. This construction avoids a CAD kernel in Python while
retaining chamber-centered section arcs and explicit rib faces.

## Choosing the rounded height input

Rounded sections accept the full internal coolant height by default. To use
its older base-height parameter, set the option on the cross section:

```python
cross_section = psf.regen.CrossSectionRounded(height_input="base")
# The same option is available on CrossSectionRoundedInternal.
```

Then `CoolingCircuit(channel_height=...)` supplies the base parameter. This
is the value used directly as `prof.h` in commit `ca6d36a`, before the switch
to full-height inputs. It excludes the rounded lobes and is distinct from the
straight-side length, which is `h_base*cos(theta/2)`.

The conversion uses the rounded section model's existing relation:

```text
q_inner = r_ref*sin(theta/2) - t_wall
H_full  = 2*q_inner + h_base*(sin(theta/2) + cos(theta/2))
```

Zero base height is valid: it produces the circular limiting section. Negative
or nonfinite heights are rejected. Full-height input must still meet the
geometric minimum `2*q_inner`.

The section exposes `full_height(profiles)` and `base_height(profiles)` in
either input mode. After chamber assembly, use
`circuit.channel_full_heights` and `circuit.channel_base_heights` for the
corresponding arrays on `circuit.x_domain`. The original `channel_height(x)`,
`channel_heights`, and design-input quantity `h` retain the supplied convention.

Height plots always default to full internal height, independently of the
input convention:

```python
psf.viz.PlotChannelHeight(thrust_chamber)                 # full height
psf.viz.PlotChannelHeight(thrust_chamber, height="base") # base height
psf.viz.PlotChannelHeight(thrust_chamber, height="both") # both, labeled

# The circuit selection option works with either representation.
plot = psf.viz.PlotChannelHeight(
    thrust_chamber, circuit_index=0, height="both"
)
report.add_tab("Channel geometry").add_figure(plot)
```

Squared channels have the same full and base height, so plotting both adds
only one trace for those circuits. The wall-layer plot also uses full height.
Native 3D and Onshape geometry use the section's selected interpretation.
Coolant-centerline placement uses full height after the local pitch has been
resolved. Equivalent base and full inputs therefore give the same section
analytics, coolant path, and construction geometry when the other resolved
design inputs agree. A helix or width law that depends on the input `h` sees
the selected convention and may require a corresponding change to that law.

## Rounded channels and Onshape

`CrossSectionRounded` and `CrossSectionRoundedInternal` retain the existing
rounded lobe geometry and base-height conversion in planes normal to the
section-reference centerline. The inner lobe bottom sits on the coolant-facing
wall. At the minimum rounded height, the two arcs form a circle and
FeatureScript omits the zero-length side lines.

The advanced example's exporter writes schema version 3. Each channel carries
`sectionType: "squared"` or `"rounded"`; each station carries its plane, two
arcs (centers, radii, start/end angles), and a circular-limit flag. FeatureScript
uses these resolved arcs and connects their ends with rib sides. Its sketch
calls follow the [Onshape sketch API](https://cad.onshape.com/FsDoc/library.html#module-sketch.fs).
It lofts and patterns each seed independently, so one document can mix the
section types. Regenerate version 2 JSON with the updated exporter.

The native viewer samples the same arcs into polygons. Its `n_arc_pts` setting
controls circumferential tessellation and `stride` controls the selected
stations; the final station is always retained. Onshape retains analytic
circular arcs and uses all exported stations. Neither the Python tests nor
the native mesh renderer execute Onshape's loft kernel.

## Assistant

Each circuit now retains its own fin setting, and an explicit `rib_material` supplies conductivity only to the fin calculation. The default remains enabled with the coolant-facing main-wall material. I’ve updated RL10 and added checks for circuits with different settings in the same chamber.

Both settings now belong to `CoolingCircuit`:

```python
CoolingCircuit(
    ...,
    enable_fin=True,
    rib_material=psf.common.solids.GRCop42,
)
```

- `enable_fin` defaults to `True`.
- Omitted `rib_material` uses the coolant-facing main-wall material.
- `ThrustChamber` no longer accepts or overrides fin settings.
- RL10 now enables fins separately on each circuit.

## User

Now we move back to the centerline question. I think we should have these: 

contour: Specifies the target gas flow area. 
coolant_reference_path: specifies the path of the cooling channel at a point practical for that speficic cross section type. For a rounded cannel it would be the center of the inner lobe, for a squared channel it would be the center of the coolant facing wall. (i believe this is how it is currently defined). Helical channels obviously also have a slant, but yeah. This centerline needs to be aware of what kind of cooling channel it has, and how thick the wall is at any point. For the rounded channel, the offset of this reference centerline needs to take into account the intended area that we talked about. A bit of math needs to be done to find the correct location for this centerline for the rounded version. The squared version is a pretty simple wall thickness offset. 

coolant_centroid_path: Defined so that the flow model has a representative path for length and curvature and such. 

I don't think there needs to be a physical hot wall path. Don't see the use of it.

- The more sensible names and definitions outlined above are used.

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
import numpy as np

from pyskyfire.regen.design_inputs import (
    DesignContext,
    contour_providers,
    make_evaluator,
)

class ChannelPlacement(ABC):
    """Abstract base class defining how coolant channels are positioned.

    Subclasses implement different placement strategies (surface, internal)
    that compute the radial coordinate of the channel centerline.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n_channel_positions : int
        Number of circumferential channel locations (“leaves”).
    channel_angular_width : callable or None, optional
        Function returning angular width [rad]. May be `None` if uniform.
    occludes : bool, optional
        Whether this placement blocks part of the wall from hot gas view.

    Attributes
    ----------
    n_channel_positions : int
        Number of circumferential positions.
    channel_angular_width : callable or None
        Angular width function or constant.
    occludes : bool
        Whether the placement occludes hot surface area.

    See Also
    --------
    SurfacePlacement
    InternalPlacement
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        n_channel_positions: int,
        channel_angular_width=None,
        occludes: bool = True,
        helix_angle=0.0,
    ):
        self.n_channel_positions = n_channel_positions   # << new home
        self.occludes = occludes

        self._channel_angular_width = channel_angular_width
        self._channel_angular_width_evaluator = (
            None
            if channel_angular_width is None
            else make_evaluator(
                channel_angular_width,
                slot="channel_angular_width",
                label=f"{type(self).__name__}.channel_angular_width",
            )
        )

        self._helix_angle = helix_angle
        self._helix_angle_evaluator = make_evaluator(
            helix_angle,
            slot="helix_angle",
            label=f"{type(self).__name__}.helix_angle",
        )

    def __setstate__(self, state):
        """Load placements serialized before the angular-width rename."""
        if (
            "channel_angular_width" not in state
            and "channel_width" in state
        ):
            state["channel_angular_width"] = state.pop("channel_width")
        state.pop("_circuit", None)
        self.__dict__.update(state)

    # ---------------- design inputs ----------------
    def _context(
        self,
        x,
        contour=None,
        circuit=None,
        *,
        include_section: bool,
    ) -> DesignContext:
        """Build the design-input context for one station.

        A placement may be shared by several circuits, so the circuit is passed
        in per call rather than stored. Without one, only tier A is available.
        """
        if circuit is not None:
            return circuit.design_context(x, include_section=include_section)
        return DesignContext(contour_providers(contour, float(x)))

    def helix_angle(self, x, contour=None, circuit=None) -> float:
        """Return the local helix angle [rad], measured from the meridian."""
        evaluator = self._helix_angle_evaluator
        if evaluator.constant_value is not None:
            return evaluator.constant_value
        # include_section reaches the channel height, which is built before any
        # helix angle is evaluated. The pitch quantities are still absent, so a
        # helix law cannot circularly depend on the pitch it sets.
        return evaluator(
            self._context(x, contour, circuit, include_section=True)
        )

    @property
    def has_channel_angular_width(self) -> bool:
        """Whether this placement defines its own angular-width law."""
        return self._channel_angular_width_evaluator is not None

    def channel_angular_width(self, x, contour=None, circuit=None) -> float:
        """Return the user-specified angular width [rad] at ``x``."""
        evaluator = self._channel_angular_width_evaluator
        if evaluator is None:
            raise AttributeError(
                f"{type(self).__name__} does not define channel_angular_width"
            )
        if evaluator.constant_value is not None:
            return evaluator.constant_value
        return evaluator(
            self._context(x, contour, circuit, include_section=True)
        )

    @abstractmethod
    def compute_centerline_radius(self,
                                  x: float,
                                  contour) -> float:
        """Return the section-reference radius ``r(x)`` for this placement.

        For surface channels this is the hot-wall radius used by the
        cross-section models.  The coolant-flow centre is obtained separately
        with :meth:`compute_flow_centerline_radius`.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def compute_flow_centerline_radius(
        self,
        x: float,
        contour,
        wall_thickness: float,
        channel_height: float,
    ) -> float:
        """Return the radius of the modeled coolant-flow centre [m].

        Placements that already describe a flow centre need no offset.  A
        surface placement overrides this because its section reference is the
        hot wall.
        """
        return self.compute_centerline_radius(x, contour)

    def channel_count(self) -> int:
        return self.n_channel_positions

    def dtheta_dx(self, x: float, contour, circuit=None) -> float:
        """Return dθ/dx [rad/m] for the representative lane centerline.
        Default: 0 (axial/vertical channels).
        """
        return 0.0

    def centerline_dtheta_dx(
        self,
        x: float,
        contour,
        flow_radius: float,
        flow_dr_dx: float,
        circuit=None,
    ) -> float:
        """Return ``dtheta/dx`` for the actual coolant-flow centreline."""
        return self.dtheta_dx(x, contour, circuit)

class SurfacePlacement(ChannelPlacement):
    """Placement model for surface-mounted cooling channels.

    Channels are positioned just outside the main wall stack,
    offset by total thickness and corrected for local contour angle.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n_channel_positions : int
        Number of channels around the circumference.

    Attributes
    ----------
    n_channel_positions : int
        Number of circumferential leaves.
    n_channels_per_leaf : int
        Fixed to 1 for surface channels.
    occludes : bool
        Always True — these channels block hot-side area.

    See Also
    --------
    ChannelPlacement
    InternalPlacement
    """
    def __init__(self, n_channel_positions: int, helix_angle=0.0):
        self.n_channels_per_leaf = 1
        super().__init__(
            n_channel_positions,
            channel_angular_width=None,
            occludes=True,
            helix_angle=helix_angle,
        )

    def compute_centerline_radius(self, x, contour):
        r_hot   = contour.r(x)
        #alpha       = contour.normal_angle(x)
        #t_total = wall_group.total_thickness(x)
        #TODO: This is approximately correct. Will want to reimplement the effect of the channel wall thickness in the future.
        return r_hot #+ t_total/np.cos(alpha)

    def compute_flow_centerline_radius(
        self,
        x,
        contour,
        wall_thickness,
        channel_height,
    ):
        """Return the coolant centroid used by the 1-D passage model.

        The section analytics construct a radial wall/channel stack, so its
        consistent flow centre is the hot-wall radius plus the complete wall
        stack and half the channel height.
        """
        return (
            self.compute_centerline_radius(x, contour)
            + float(wall_thickness)
            + 0.5 * float(channel_height)
        )

    def dtheta_dx(self, x, contour, circuit=None):
        gamma = self.helix_angle(x, contour, circuit)
        r = self.compute_centerline_radius(x, contour)
        drdx = contour.dr_dx(x)
        # guard r≈0 near axis (should not happen for chamber wall, but robust)
        r = max(1e-12, r)
        return np.tan(gamma) * np.sqrt(1.0 + drdx**2) / r

    def centerline_dtheta_dx(
        self,
        x,
        contour,
        flow_radius,
        flow_dr_dx,
        circuit=None,
    ):
        """Honor the requested helix angle on the coolant-flow centreline.

        ``gamma`` is measured from the local meridional direction.  Therefore
        ``tan(gamma) = r dtheta / ds_meridional``.
        """
        gamma = self.helix_angle(x, contour, circuit)
        radius = max(abs(float(flow_radius)), 1e-12)
        return (
            np.tan(gamma)
            * np.sqrt(1.0 + float(flow_dr_dx) ** 2)
            / radius
        )

def _placement_slope_data(thrust_chamber, centerlines, circuit_ids):
    desired_slopes = []
    slope_starts = []
    slope_ends = []
    contour = thrust_chamber.contour
    for centerline, circuit_index in zip(centerlines, circuit_ids, strict=True):
        circuit = thrust_chamber.cooling_circuits[circuit_index]
        placement = circuit.placement
        axial = centerline[:, 0]
        slope = np.asarray(
            [placement.dtheta_dx(float(x), contour, circuit) for x in axial],
            dtype=float,
        )
        desired_slopes.append(slope)
        slope_starts.append(float(slope[0]))
        slope_ends.append(float(slope[-1]))
    return desired_slopes, slope_starts, slope_ends


def resolve_numerical_layout(thrust_chamber, **solver_options) -> ChannelLayout:
    """Resolve the historical numerical packing layout.

    The result stores only the unique seeds in the greatest-common-divisor
    wedge.  Consumers may call :meth:`ChannelLayout.expanded_channels` when
    they need all physical instances.
    """

    centerlines, widths, circuit_ids, metadata = collect_channels(thrust_chamber)
    if not centerlines:
        return ChannelLayout("numerical", (), metadata)
    desired_slopes, slope_starts, slope_ends = _placement_slope_data(
        thrust_chamber,
        centerlines,
        circuit_ids,
    )
    options = {
        "k_pack": 2.0,
        "k_bend": 0.1,
        "k_slope": 0.05,
        "desired_slope": desired_slopes,
        "dt": 0.15,
        "tol": 1.0e-5,
        "max_iters": 800,
        "gamma_damp": 0.4,
        "wedge_angle": metadata["wedge_angle"] if metadata["g"] > 1 else None,
        "endpoint_slope0": slope_starts,
        "endpoint_slopeN": slope_ends,
    }
    options.update(solver_options)
    resolved = redistribute_channels(
        centerlines,
        widths,
        **options,
    )

    seed_numbers: dict[int, int] = {}
    channels = []
    for centerline, circuit_index in zip(resolved, circuit_ids, strict=True):
        seed_index = seed_numbers.get(circuit_index, 0)
        seed_numbers[circuit_index] = seed_index + 1
        circuit = thrust_chamber.cooling_circuits[circuit_index]
        channels.append(
            ResolvedChannel(
                name=f"{circuit.name}_seed_{seed_index}",
                circuit_index=circuit_index,
                seed_index=seed_index,
                centerline=centerline,
                pattern_count=metadata["g"],
                pattern_angle_rad=metadata["wedge_angle"],
            )
        )
    return ChannelLayout("numerical", tuple(channels), metadata)

    # ---------------- design-input contexts ----------------
    def bind_chamber(self, chamber):
        """Attach the owning chamber, which supplies cross-circuit counts."""
        self._chamber = chamber

    def _channels_all_circuits_provider(self, x):
        def provider():
            if self._chamber is None:
                raise DesignInputError(
                    f"{self.name}: 'n_channels_all_circuits' counts channels "
                    "across every circuit, so it is only available once the "
                    "circuit belongs to a ThrustChamber"
                )
            return float(self._chamber.number_of_channels(x, occluding_only=True))

        return provider

    def _section_provider_values(self, x):
        """Interpolate whichever section quantities have been built at ``x``.

        Anything not built yet comes back as ``None`` and is then omitted from
        the context, which is what makes the later part of tier C unavailable
        to slots that are evaluated earlier in the geometry build.
        """
        if self.x_domain is None:
            return None
        heights = self.channel_heights
        local_sector = getattr(self, "channel_local_sector", None)
        gamma = self.helix_angle_vals
        return {
            "h": (
                None
                if heights is None
                else float(np.interp(x, self.x_domain, heights))
            ),
            "theta": (
                None
                if local_sector is None
                else float(np.interp(x, self.x_domain, local_sector))
            ),
            "gamma": (
                None if gamma is None else float(np.interp(x, self.x_domain, gamma))
            ),
        }

    def design_context(self, x, *, include_section: bool) -> DesignContext:
        """Build the design-input context for this circuit at ``x``."""
        x = float(x)
        providers = contour_providers(self.contour, x)
        providers.update(
            layout_providers(
                n_channel_positions=int(self.placement.n_channel_positions),
                n_channels=int(self.n_channels),
                n_channels_all_circuits=self._channels_all_circuits_provider(x),
                t_wall=lambda: float(self.channel_wall_thickness(x)),
                t_wall_total=lambda: float(self.total_thickness(x)),
                t_hot_layer=lambda: float(self.hot_side_layer_thickness(x)),
            )
        )
        if include_section:
            section = self._section_provider_values(x)
            if section is not None:
                providers.update(
                    section_providers(
                        r=float(self.contour.r(x)),
                        h=section["h"],
                        gamma=section["gamma"],
                        theta=section["theta"],
                        t_wall=float(self.channel_wall_thickness(x)),
                    )
                )
        return DesignContext(providers)

    def _evaluate(self, evaluator, x, *, include_section: bool):
        """Evaluate a design input over a scalar or array of ``x``."""
        constant = evaluator.constant_value
        values = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
        if constant is not None:
            if values.ndim:
                return np.full(values.shape, constant, dtype=float)
            return constant
        result = np.array(
            [
                evaluator(
                    self.design_context(value, include_section=include_section)
                )
                for value in values.ravel()
            ],
            dtype=float,
        ).reshape(values.shape)
        return float(result) if result.ndim == 0 else result

    # ---------------- design inputs ----------------
    def channel_height(self, x):
        """Return the supplied height [m], using the section's input convention.

        Use ``channel_full_heights`` or ``channel_base_heights`` to report
        resolved physical heights on ``x_domain`` after chamber assembly.
        """
        return self._evaluate(
            self._channel_height_evaluator, x, include_section=False
        )

    def roughness(self, x):
        """Return the absolute channel roughness [m] at ``x``."""
        return self._evaluate(self._roughness_evaluator, x, include_section=True)

    def hot_gas_surface_area_multiplier(self, x):
        """Return the circuit-specific effective hot-side area multiplier."""
        values = np.asarray(
            self._evaluate(
                self._hot_gas_surface_area_multiplier_evaluator,
                x,
                include_section=True,
            ),
            dtype=float,
        )
        if not np.all(np.isfinite(values)) or np.any(values <= 0.0):
            raise ValueError(
                f"{self.name}: hot_gas_surface_area_multiplier must return "
                "finite, positive values"
            )
        return float(values) if values.ndim == 0 else values

    def _wall_thickness(self, x, role=None):
        thickness = np.zeros_like(np.asarray(x, dtype=float))
        for wall in self.walls:
            if role is None or getattr(wall, "role", "main") == role:
                thickness = thickness + np.asarray(wall.thickness(x), dtype=float)
        return float(thickness) if thickness.ndim == 0 else thickness

    def total_thickness(self, x):
        """Return the full hot-to-coolant stack thickness, including liners."""
        return self._wall_thickness(x)

    def channel_wall_thickness(self, x):
        """Return the combined main-wall thickness used for channel geometry."""
        return self._wall_thickness(x, role="main")

    def hot_side_layer_thickness(self, x):
        """Return the combined thickness of explicitly marked hot-side liners."""
        return self._wall_thickness(x, role="liner")

    # ---------------- profiles bundle ----------------
    def _prof(self, centerline: np.ndarray) -> SectionProfiles:
        """
        Build a SectionProfiles with trivial frames (analytics don't use them).
        """
        x = centerline[:, 0]

        # All main layers contribute to arc/ligament thickness. Hot-side
        # liners offset the reference but do not form the tube walls.
        t_channel_wall = self.channel_wall_thickness(x)

        return SectionProfiles(
            h=np.asarray(self.channel_heights, float),
            theta=np.asarray(self.channel_local_sector, float),
            # theta=np.asarray(self.channel_angular_width, float),
            t_wall=np.asarray(t_channel_wall, float),
            centerline=np.asarray(centerline, float),
            **self._design_input_context(x),
        )

    def _design_input_context(self, x):
        """Return the optional ``SectionProfiles`` fields, best effort.

        Everything here only feeds design-input functions. A quantity that
        cannot be determined is left out rather than raising, so that a
        partially built circuit can still be asked for plain geometry; a
        design input that needs the missing quantity is what raises.
        """
        self.build_channel_angular_widths()

        # A rounded base input only resolves to full height once the local
        # pitch is known. Build its coolant path before computing
        # length, curvature, or volume. The reference/layout path is unchanged.
        for circuit in self.cooling_circuits:
            if getattr(circuit.cross_section, "height_input", "full") == "base":
                self._build_coolant_centerline(circuit, circuit.channel_full_heights)

        # --- per-circuit preprocessing for solver ---
        for circuit in self.cooling_circuits:
            circuit.finalize()

        # --- hot-gas side (optional/on-demand) ---
        if compute_gas and hasattr(
            self.combustion_transport, "compute_aerothermodynamics"
        ):
            self.combustion_transport.compute_aerothermodynamics(self.contour)

        self.film_cooling = film_cooling
        if self.film_cooling is not None:
            self.film_cooling.x = self._resolve_signed_fraction_to_x(
                self.film_cooling.x_fraction
            )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Domain → centerline → section scalars (sim-only)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def build_circuit_x_domain(self):
        """
        Convert each circuit's fractional span into an x-grid whose size
        scales with the fraction of the overall contour length covered.
        Uses at least 3 nodes per circuit.
        """
        x_min = float(self.contour.xs[0])
        x_max = float(self.contour.xs[-1])
        L_tot = max(1e-30, x_max - x_min)  # guard zero-length contours

        MIN_NODES = 3

        for circuit in self.cooling_circuits:
            f0, f1 = circuit.span

            # Map signed fractional spans to absolute x, keeping your original convention
            x0 = f0 * (x_max if f0 >= 0.0 else -x_min)
            x1 = f1 * (x_max if f1 >= 0.0 else -x_min)

            L_seg = abs(x1 - x0)
            frac = L_seg / L_tot
            n_here = max(MIN_NODES, int(round(self.n_nodes * frac)))

            if x0 <= x1:
                x_domain = np.linspace(x0, x1, n_here)
            else:
                # reversed span: keep coolant marching direction by reversing
                x_domain = np.linspace(x1, x0, n_here)[::-1]

            circuit.set_x_domain(x_domain)

    def build_channel_centerlines(self):
        if not self.cooling_circuits:
            return

        # Use one integration grid for the reference angular laws while
        # retaining each circuit's independent simulation grid. Thus equal
        # placement laws produce the same underlying reference path without
        # changing any transport discretization.
        shared_reference_x = np.unique(
            np.concatenate(
                [
                    np.asarray(circuit.x_domain, dtype=float)
                    for circuit in self.cooling_circuits
                ]
            )
        )

        for circuit in self.cooling_circuits:
            xs = circuit.x_domain

            # The cross-section models use a wall/surface reference, whereas
            # length and curvature must follow the coolant centroid.
            section_radii = np.array(
                [
                    circuit.placement.compute_centerline_radius(x, self.contour)
                    for x in xs
                ],
                dtype=float,
            )
            section_radii += np.asarray(
                circuit.hot_side_layer_thickness(xs),
                dtype=float,
            )
            reference_x = shared_reference_x
            section_dtheta_dx = np.array(
                [
                    circuit.placement.dtheta_dx(x, self.contour, circuit)
                    for x in reference_x
                ],
                dtype=float,
            )

            # The section-reference curve owns the CAD/layout angular path.
            reference_theta = np.zeros_like(reference_x, dtype=float)
            reference_theta[1:] = np.cumsum(
                0.5
                * (section_dtheta_dx[1:] + section_dtheta_dx[:-1])
                * (reference_x[1:] - reference_x[:-1])
            )
            section_theta = np.interp(xs, reference_x, reference_theta)
            self_theta_origin = float(section_theta[0])
            section_theta -= self_theta_origin
            circuit.section_reference_theta_origin_rad = self_theta_origin

            circuit.helix_angle_vals = np.array(
                [
                    circuit.placement.helix_angle(x, self.contour, circuit)
                    for x in xs
                ],
                dtype=float,
            )
            circuit.is_helical = bool(np.any(np.abs(circuit.helix_angle_vals) > 1e-12))

            circuit.set_centerline(
                [np.column_stack([xs, section_radii, section_theta])]
            )
            if getattr(circuit.cross_section, "height_input", "full") != "base":
                self._build_coolant_centerline(circuit, circuit.channel_heights)

    def _build_coolant_centerline(self, circuit, channel_heights):
        """Build the transport path using resolved full channel heights."""
        xs = circuit.x_domain
        wall_thicknesses = np.asarray(
            circuit.total_thickness(xs),
            dtype=float,
        )
        flow_radii = np.array(
            [
                circuit.placement.compute_flow_centerline_radius(
                    x,
                    self.contour,
                    wall_thickness,
                    channel_height,
                )
                for x, wall_thickness, channel_height in zip(
                    xs,
                    wall_thicknesses,
                    channel_heights,
                )
            ],
            dtype=float,
        )
        # Transport length and curvature use a distinct coolant-centroid
        # curve. It honors the requested helix angle at its own radius but
        # never participates in analytical layout validation.
        flow_dr_dx = np.gradient(flow_radii, xs, edge_order=2)
        flow_dtheta_dx = np.array(
            [
                circuit.placement.centerline_dtheta_dx(
                    x,
                    self.contour,
                    flow_radius,
                    dr_dx,
                    circuit,
                )
                for x, flow_radius, dr_dx in zip(
                    xs,
                    flow_radii,
                    flow_dr_dx,
                    strict=True,
                )
            ],
            dtype=float,
        )
        flow_theta = np.zeros_like(xs, dtype=float)
        flow_theta[1:] = np.cumsum(
            0.5 * (flow_dtheta_dx[1:] + flow_dtheta_dx[:-1]) * (xs[1:] - xs[:-1])
        )

        circuit.set_coolant_centerline(
            [np.column_stack([xs, flow_radii, flow_theta])]
        )

    def build_channel_angular_widths(self):
        """
        Compute wedge angle (theta) arrays used by cross-section analytics.

        Priority:
        1) If placement provides channel_angular_width(x), use it.
        2) If placement is 'internal' (non-occluding), use height as an angular-width proxy.
        3) Otherwise, default to an even packing among surface-occluding channels:
           theta(x) = 2π / n_occ(x), where n_occ is provided by the circuit group.
        """
        for circuit in self.cooling_circuits:
            xs = circuit.x_domain
            p = circuit.placement

            if p.has_channel_angular_width:
                angular_widths = np.array(
                    [p.channel_angular_width(x, self.contour, circuit) for x in xs],
                    dtype=float,
                )
                local_sector = angular_widths.copy()

            elif getattr(p, "occludes", True) is False:
                # internal / non-occluding: use height as an angular proxy (sim only)
                angular_widths = np.array(
                    [circuit.channel_height(x) for x in xs],
                    dtype=float,
                )
                local_sector = angular_widths.copy()

            else:
                # uniform angular share among all occluding channels present at x
                n_occ = np.array(
                    [self.number_of_channels(x, occluding_only=True) for x in xs],
                    dtype=float,
                )
                gamma = np.array(
                    [p.helix_angle(x, self.contour, circuit) for x in xs],
                    dtype=float,
                )
                # print
                angular_widths = np.where(
                    n_occ > 0.0,
                    2.0 * np.pi / n_occ,
                    0.0,
                )
                local_sector = np.where(
                    n_occ > 0.0, 2.0 * np.pi * np.cos(gamma) / n_occ, 0.0
                )  # multiplying with cos gamma for helical implementation

            circuit.set_channel_angular_width(angular_widths)
            circuit.set_channel_local_sector(local_sector)

    def build_channel_heights(self):
        """Evaluate the per-circuit height law h(x) on each circuit domain."""
        for circuit in self.cooling_circuits:
            xs = circuit.x_domain
            h = np.array([circuit.channel_height(x) for x in xs], dtype=float)
            circuit.set_channel_height(h)

def _overlap_components(circuits, *, tolerance: float) -> list[list[int]]:
    occluding = [
        index
        for index, circuit in enumerate(circuits)
        if bool(getattr(circuit.placement, "occludes", True))
    ]
    spans = {index: _axial_span(circuits[index]) for index in occluding}
    adjacency = {index: set() for index in occluding}
    for position, first in enumerate(occluding):
        for second in occluding[position + 1 :]:
            if _positive_overlap(spans[first], spans[second], tolerance):
                adjacency[first].add(second)
                adjacency[second].add(first)

    components = []
    unseen = set(occluding)
    while unseen:
        start = min(unseen)
        stack = [start]
        component = []
        unseen.remove(start)
        while stack:
            current = stack.pop()
            component.append(current)
            for neighbor in sorted(adjacency[current], reverse=True):
                if neighbor in unseen:
                    unseen.remove(neighbor)
                    stack.append(neighbor)
        components.append(sorted(component))

    for index in range(len(circuits)):
        if index not in occluding:
            components.append([index])
    return sorted(components, key=lambda component: component[0])


def _validate_matching_angular_evolution(
    first,
    second,
    *,
    span_tolerance: float,
    angular_rate_tolerance: float,
) -> float:
    """Validate the nominal section-reference laws and return their phase gap."""
    first_centerline = np.asarray(first.centerlines[0], dtype=float)
    second_centerline = np.asarray(second.centerlines[0], dtype=float)
    lower = max(_axial_span(first)[0], _axial_span(second)[0])
    upper = min(_axial_span(first)[1], _axial_span(second)[1])
    if upper - lower <= span_tolerance:
        return 0.0

    samples = np.unique(
        np.concatenate(
            (
                first_centerline[
                    (first_centerline[:, 0] >= lower)
                    & (first_centerline[:, 0] <= upper),
                    0,
                ],
                second_centerline[
                    (second_centerline[:, 0] >= lower)
                    & (second_centerline[:, 0] <= upper),
                    0,
                ],
                np.array([lower, upper]),
            )
        )
    )
    first_rate = np.asarray(
        [
            first.placement.dtheta_dx(float(x), getattr(first, "contour", None), first)
            for x in samples
        ]
    )
    second_rate = np.asarray(
        [
            second.placement.dtheta_dx(float(x), getattr(second, "contour", None), second)
            for x in samples
        ]
    )
    if not np.allclose(
        first_rate,
        second_rate,
        atol=angular_rate_tolerance,
        rtol=0.0,
    ):
        raise AnalyticalLayoutError(
            f"Circuits {first.name!r} and {second.name!r} do not follow the "
            "same angular/helix evolution over their overlap"
        )

    first_origin = getattr(first, "section_reference_theta_origin_rad", None)
    second_origin = getattr(second, "section_reference_theta_origin_rad", None)
    if first_origin is not None and second_origin is not None:
        return float(first_origin) - float(second_origin)

    def reference_angle_at(centerline, x):
        order = np.argsort(centerline[:, 0])
        axial = centerline[order, 0]
        angles = np.unwrap(centerline[order, 2])
        return float(np.interp(x, axial, angles))

    first_angle = reference_angle_at(first_centerline, lower)
    second_angle = reference_angle_at(second_centerline, lower)
    return second_angle - first_angle


def resolve_analytical_layout(
    thrust_chamber,
    *,
    span_tolerance: float = 1.0e-9,
    angular_rate_tolerance: float = 1.0e-7,
) -> ChannelLayout:
    """Resolve an exact nominal layout using only constant phase rotations.

    Overlapping, occluding circuits are inferred to interleave.  Such circuits
    must have equal channel counts and matching section-reference angular
    rates.  The coolant-centroid path is intentionally ignored.  Two may
    have different axial endpoints; groups of three or more must have identical
    spans.  The first circuit has zero added phase and later circuits divide a
    single channel pitch evenly.
    """

    circuits = thrust_chamber.cooling_circuits
    if not circuits:
        return ChannelLayout("analytical", (), {"groups": []})
    for circuit in circuits:
        if circuit.centerlines is None or not circuit.centerlines:
            raise AnalyticalLayoutError(
                f"Circuit {circuit.name!r} has no section-reference centerline"
            )

    groups = _overlap_components(circuits, tolerance=span_tolerance)
    phases: dict[int, float] = {}
    group_metadata = []
    for group in groups:
        counts = [int(circuits[index].placement.n_channel_positions) for index in group]
        if len(set(counts)) != 1:
            names = ", ".join(repr(circuits[index].name) for index in group)
            raise AnalyticalLayoutError(
                f"Interleaving circuits must have equal channel counts: {names}"
            )

        if len(group) >= 3:
            reference_span = _axial_span(circuits[group[0]])
            for index in group[1:]:
                if not np.allclose(
                    _axial_span(circuits[index]),
                    reference_span,
                    atol=span_tolerance,
                    rtol=0.0,
                ):
                    names = ", ".join(repr(circuits[item].name) for item in group)
                    raise AnalyticalLayoutError(
                        "Three or more interleaving circuits must have identical "
                        f"axial spans: {names}"
                    )

        nominal_phase_from_first = {group[0]: 0.0}
        for position, first_index in enumerate(group):
            for second_index in group[position + 1 :]:
                phase_difference = _validate_matching_angular_evolution(
                    circuits[first_index],
                    circuits[second_index],
                    span_tolerance=span_tolerance,
                    angular_rate_tolerance=angular_rate_tolerance,
                )
                if first_index == group[0]:
                    nominal_phase_from_first[second_index] = phase_difference

        count = counts[0]
        combined_pitch = TWO_PI / (count * len(group))
        for phase_index, circuit_index in enumerate(group):
            phases[circuit_index] = (
                phase_index * combined_pitch
                - nominal_phase_from_first.get(circuit_index, 0.0)
            )
        group_metadata.append(
            {
                "circuit_indices": list(group),
                "channel_count": count,
                "phase_step_rad": combined_pitch,
            }
        )

    channels = []
    for circuit_index, circuit in enumerate(circuits):
        count = int(circuit.placement.n_channel_positions)
        phase = phases[circuit_index]
        centerline = rotate_cylindrical_centerline(circuit.centerlines[0], phase)
        channels.append(
            ResolvedChannel(
                name=f"{circuit.name}_seed_0",
                circuit_index=circuit_index,
                seed_index=0,
                centerline=centerline,
                pattern_count=count,
                pattern_angle_rad=TWO_PI / count,
                angular_offset_rad=phase,
            )
        )

    return ChannelLayout(
        method="analytical",
        channels=tuple(channels),
        metadata={"groups": group_metadata},
    )

    contour = psf.regen.Contour(xs, rs, name="Methane Engine")

    copper_wall = psf.regen.Wall(
        material=params["copper"],
        thickness=params["copper_thickness"],
    )

    def fuel_channel_height(x):
        return (
            params["fuel_throat_channel_height"]
            + params["fuel_channel_height_slope"] * abs(x)
        )

    ox_outbound_span = (0.11, 1.0)
    ox_return_span = (1.0, 0.21)

    def span_fraction_to_x(span_fraction):
        if span_fraction >= 0.0:
            return span_fraction * float(contour.xs[-1])
        return span_fraction * -float(contour.xs[0])

    ox_outbound_bounds = tuple(map(span_fraction_to_x, ox_outbound_span))
    ox_return_bounds = tuple(map(span_fraction_to_x, ox_return_span))
    ox_overlap_start = max(min(ox_outbound_bounds), min(ox_return_bounds))

    def ox_channel_height(x):
        if x < ox_overlap_start:
            return params["ox_single_pass_channel_height"]
        return params["ox_channel_height"]

    cross_section_squared = psf.regen.CrossSectionSquared(
        rib_width=1e-3,
    )

    cross_section_rounded = psf.regen.CrossSectionRounded(height_input="base")
    fuel_transport = psf.skycea.CoolantTransport(params["coolprop_fu"])
    ox_transport = psf.skycea.CoolantTransport(params["coolprop_ox"])

    # An area-preserving helix.
    #
    # A squared section holds A = h * [(pi*cos(gamma)/n) * (2*r_base + h) - rib],
    # so with the channel height, rib width and channel count fixed, the area is
    # constant exactly when cos(gamma) * (2*r_base + h) is. Anchoring that
    # product where the nozzle circuits begin pins the helix at 20 deg there and
    # opens it out as the nozzle radius grows, instead of letting the passage
    # swell with the wall it wraps.
    # The law is written against the nozzle's design height rather than the
    # local one. Both ox circuits share this placement, and the analytical
    # layout requires them to follow a single angular evolution, so the helix
    # must not depend on anything that differs between them.
    helix_start_x = min(ox_outbound_bounds)
    helix_design_height = params["ox_channel_height"]
    helix_reference = np.cos(np.radians(20.0)) * (
        2.0
        * (
            contour.r(helix_start_x)
            + float(copper_wall.thickness(helix_start_x))
        )
        + helix_design_height
    )

    def area_preserving_helix(r, t_wall):
        """Return the helix angle that holds the coolant area constant [rad]."""
        return float(np.arccos(np.clip(helix_reference / (2.0 * (r + t_wall) + helix_design_height), -1.0, 1.0,)))

    fuel_channel_placement = psf.regen.SurfacePlacement(n_channel_positions=params["fuel_channel_count"],)
    nozzle_channel_placement = psf.regen.SurfacePlacement(
        n_channel_positions=params["nozzle_channel_count"],
        helix_angle=area_preserving_helix,
    )

    fuel_chamber_pass = psf.regen.CoolingCircuit(
        name="Fuel Chamber Pass",
        contour=contour,
        coolant_transport=fuel_transport,
        cross_section=cross_section_rounded,
        span=[0.1, -1.0],
        placement=fuel_channel_placement,
        walls=[copper_wall],
        roughness=params["copper_roughness_height"],
        channel_height=fuel_channel_height,
        hot_gas_surface_area_multiplier=params[
            "fuel_hot_gas_surface_area_multiplier"
        ],
    )

    ox_nozzle_pass_outbound = psf.regen.CoolingCircuit(
        name="Oxidizer Nozzle Pass Outbound",
        contour=contour,
        coolant_transport=ox_transport,
        cross_section=cross_section_rounded,
        span=ox_outbound_span,
        placement=nozzle_channel_placement,
        walls=[copper_wall],
        roughness=params["copper_roughness_height"],
        channel_height=ox_channel_height,
        hot_gas_surface_area_multiplier=params[
            "ox_outbound_hot_gas_surface_area_multiplier"
        ],
    )

    ox_nozzle_pass_return = psf.regen.CoolingCircuit(
        name="Oxidizer Nozzle Pass Return",
        contour=contour,
        coolant_transport=ox_transport,
        cross_section=cross_section_squared,
        span=ox_return_span,
        placement=nozzle_channel_placement,
        walls=[copper_wall],
        roughness=params["copper_roughness_height"],
        channel_height=ox_channel_height,
        hot_gas_surface_area_multiplier=params[
            "ox_return_hot_gas_surface_area_multiplier"
        ],
    )

    return psf.regen.ThrustChamber(
        contour=contour,
        combustion_transport=aerothermodynamics,

The three definitions make sense. **There is one helix convention we should settle before I refactor**, because it affects whether neighboring channels remain aligned.

The intended meanings would be:

| Name | Definition |
|---|---|
| `contour` | Ideal contour specifying the target gas-flow area. |
| `coolant_reference_path` | Inner-lobe center for rounded channels; midpoint across the coolant-facing floor for squared channels. |
| `coolant_centroid_path` | Path derived from the coolant section’s centroid, used for flow length and curvature. |

The squared reference currently sits beneath the channel wall, so moving it onto the coolant-facing floor is an intentional geometry change. The wall thickness must then be applied during reference-path construction, and removed from the downstream formulas that currently add it.

We don’t need a separate public hot-wall path. The rounded placement calculation does need to evaluate the gas-facing boundary internally to calculate its enclosed area.

**The rounded placement math works cleanly for straight, identical tubes.** I derived the area-preserving placement and checked it by independently integrating the gas area. For your cylindrical injector section:

| Quantity | Corrected value |
|---|---:|
| Ideal contour radius | 83.744534 mm |
| Inner-lobe center radius | 85.252999 mm |
| Coolant-lobe radius | 1.312912 mm |
| Neighboring coolant-passage gap | **1.200000 mm** |

That arrangement preserves the target gas area exactly for this case. The lobes are sized at their final center radius, and no subsequent translation is needed.

**The complication is how we define `helix_angle`.** At different radii, paths sharing the same angular progression generally have different helix angles. Conversely, prescribing the same helix angle independently at different radii makes their angular positions drift apart. This matters for the advanced example’s interleaved rounded and squared channels.

The existing code also independently integrates the reference and centroid helices. That should change: the centroid path should be derived from the constructed channel, so it represents that same passage.

My recommendation is to **retain `helix_angle` as the nominal angle on the ideal contour**, which determines the placement’s winding. Reference and centroid paths would then follow the constructed geometry, with their actual local angles calculated from their derivatives. This preserves a shared winding for interleaved circuits without introducing another public path.

For sloping and helical channels, the area calculation must use sections perpendicular to the engine axis, and spacing calculations must account for the actual winding. The cylindrical correction alone won’t resolve every helical CAD discrepancy.

Should I use that contour-based nominal helix convention, or do you want `helix_angle` to specify the actual angle at `coolant_reference_path`, requiring different angle laws where interleaved reference paths have different radii?

r_top = self._radii(prof)\n        w = self.rib_width(prof)\n        return 0.5 * prof.theta * (r_top**2 - r_base**2) - w * prof.h\n\n    def P_wetted(self, prof: SectionProfiles) -> np.ndarray:\n (r_top * prof.theta - w) + 2.0 * prof.h\n\n    def Dh_coolant(self, prof: SectionProfiles) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Compute hydraulic diameter [m].\"\"\"\n        return 4.0 * footprint is excluded because the heat entering it is carried\n        by the fin term in :meth:`R_coolant_per_len` rather than by the\n        channel floor.\n        \"\"\"\n        r_hot, _, _ = self._radii(prof)\n        return np.maximum(r_hot * prof.theta - self.rib_width(prof), 0.0)\n\n    def P_coolant(self, prof: SectionProfiles) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Return the channel-floor perimeter wetted by coolant [m].\"\"\"\n        _, r_base, _ = self._radii(prof)\n        return r_base * prof.theta - self.rib_width(prof)\n\n    def R_coolant_per_len(\n        self,\n        prof: per channel)\n        - Effective perimeter = P_base + eta_f * P_fin\n        - R_s = 1 / (h_c * P_eff)\n\n        Because the rib has a constant thickness, its fin-root thickness is\n        exactly area = 2*h, treated as an equivalent coolant-side perimeter.\n        h = prof.h\n        P_fin = 2.0 * h\n\n        t_rib = np.maximum(self.rib_width(prof), 1e-9)\n\n        # representative conductivity (allow scalar or array)\n        k = np.asarray(k_wall, dtype=float)\n        if k.ndim == 0:\n            k = np.full_like(h, float(k))\n\n        # Fin efficiency (adiabatic tip) for a     P_eff = np.maximum(P_base + eta * P_fin, 1e-30)\n\n        return 1.0 / (h_c * P_eff)\n\n\n# ===================== Rounded implementation ===============================\nclass _RoundedGeometryMixin:\n    \"\"\"Shared interpretation of full or legacy base-height inputs.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, n_points: int = 16, *, height_input: str = \"full\"):\n        if height_input not in (\"full\", \"base\"):\n            raise ValueError(\"height_input must be 'full' or 'base'\")\n        super().__init__(n_points=n_points)\n        self._height_input = height_input\n\n    @property\n    def height_input(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Interpretation of ``SectionProfiles.h`` (defaults for older pickles).\"\"\"\n        return getattr(self, \"_height_input\", \"full\")\n\n    def _beta_alpha(self, theta: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:\n        \"\"\"Return the inner (β) and outer (α) complementary angles.\"\"\"\n        beta = (np.pi - theta) * 0.5\n        alpha = np.pi - beta\n        return beta, alpha\n\n    def minimum_channel_height(self, prof: SectionProfiles) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Return the smallest A base height of zero is retained as the valid,\n        completely round limiting case.\n        \"\"\"\n        minimum = self.minimum_channel_height(prof)\n        invalid_radius = ~np.isfinite(minimum) | (minimum <= 0.0)\n        if np.any(invalid_radius):\n            i = int(np.flatnonzero(invalid_radius)[0])\n            raise ValueError(\n                \"rounded channel inner arc radius must be positive; prof.t_wall)**2 * 2 * beta\n        A2 = 0.5 * (r2 - prof.t_wall)**2 * 2 * alpha\n        S1 = (r1 - prof.t_wall) * L_side\n        S2 = (r2 - prof.t_wall) * L_side\n        return A1 + A2 + S1 + S2\n\n    def Dh_coolant(self, prof: SectionProfiles) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Compute hydraulic diameter [m].\"\"\"\n        A = self.A_coolant(prof)\n        r = prof.centerline[:, 1]\n        h_base = self.base_height(prof)\n        r1 = r * np.sin(prof.theta/2)\n        r2 = (r + h_base) * np.sin(prof.theta/2)\n        beta, alpha = self._beta_alpha(prof.theta)\n        L_side = h_base * np.cos(prof.theta/2)\n        arc1 = (r1 - Yes—these names make the distinctions clear:

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `contour` | Ideal geometry defining the target gas-flow area. |
| `reference_path` | A path on the ideal contour, following the nominal helix law. No wall-thickness or section-specific offset. |
| `cross_section_base_point_path` | The physical section anchor: inner-lobe center for rounded channels, or midpoint across the coolant-facing floor for squared channels. |
| `cooling_channel_centroid_path` | The coolant section’s centroid traced along the constructed channel, used for length and curvature. |

With zero helix, `reference_path` follows the contour at a fixed azimuth. Different channel types sharing the same nominal helix law share its angular progression.

The important dependency is that **the base-point and centroid paths are derived from the same channel geometry**. Neither should independently integrate another helix law. Their actual local angles can differ because their positions differ.

For rounded channels, the area-preserving placement determines the base-point position, and the lobe dimensions must use that resolved position. The centroid then follows from the resulting coolant cross section.

No additional public hot-wall path is needed.

    def __setstate__(self, state):

        if "channel_angular_width" not in state and "channel_width" in state:

        if self.centerlines is None:
            raise RuntimeError("centerlines not set")
        section_centerline = self.centerlines[0]
        flow_centerline = (
            self.coolant_centerlines[0]
            if self.coolant_centerlines is not None
            else section_centerline

        self.dA_dx_thermal_coolant_vals = cold_perimeter * self.ds_dx_vals

        # interpolate section scalars
        h = float(np.interp(x, self.x_domain, self.channel_heights))
        theta = float(np.interp(x, self.x_domain, self.channel_local_sector))
        t_wall = float(
            np.interp(
                x,
                self.x_domain,
                self.channel_wall_thickness(self.x_domain),
            )
        )

        gamma = (
            None
            if self.helix_angle_vals is None
            else np.array(
                [float(np.interp(x, self.x_domain, self.helix_angle_vals))],
                dtype=float,
            )
        )

        self.volume = abs(float(volume_per_channel)) * self.n_channels

    # ---------------- setters ----------------
    def set_centerline(self, centerline_list):
        """
        Provide one or more centerlines as arrays of shape (N, 3): [x, r, theta].
        For simulation we use the first as the representative path.
        """
        self.centerlines = [np.asarray(cl, float) for cl in centerline_list]

    def section_planes(self, centerline=None, *, axis_normal=False):
        """Lazily build planes along a section-reference centerline.

        The calculation lives in :mod:`pyskyfire.regen.channel_helpers` so the
        simulation object retains only its inexpensive centerline arrays.  By
        default this uses the circuit's nominal section reference, deliberately
        not the coolant-flow centroid used for path length and curvature.
        Set ``axis_normal=True`` for transverse squared-channel construction.
        """

        from pyskyfire.regen.channel_helpers import (
            build_axis_normal_section_planes,
            build_section_planes,
        )

        if centerline is None:
            if self.centerlines is None or not self.centerlines:
                raise RuntimeError("centerlines not set")
            centerline = self.centerlines[0]
        builder = build_axis_normal_section_planes if axis_normal else build_section_planes
        return builder(centerline)

    def set_coolant_centerline(self, centerline_list):
        """Set modeled coolant-flow-centre curves ``[x, r, theta]``."""
        self.coolant_centerlines = [np.asarray(cl, float) for cl in centerline_list]

    def set_channel_angular_width(self, angular_widths_rad):
        self.channel_angular_width = np.asarray(angular_widths_rad, float)

    def set_channel_local_sector(self, local_sectors):
        self.channel_local_sector = np.asarray(local_sectors, float)

    def set_channel_height(self, heights):
        self.channel_heights = np.asarray(heights, float)

    @property
    def channel_full_heights(self):
        """Full internal coolant heights on ``x_domain`` [m], for reporting."""
        converter = getattr(self.cross_section, "full_height", None)
        if converter is None:
            return np.asarray(self.channel_heights, float).copy()
        return converter(self._prof(self.centerlines[0]))

    @property
    def channel_base_heights(self):
        """Rounded base heights on ``x_domain`` [m]; full heights for squared."""
        converter = getattr(self.cross_section, "base_height", None)
        if converter is None:
            return np.asarray(self.channel_heights, float).copy()
        return converter(self._prof(self.centerlines[0]))

    def set_x_domain(self, x_domain):
        self.x_domain = np.asarray(x_domain, float)

    def finalize(self):
        self.precompute_thermal_properties()
        self.n_nodes = int(n_nodes)
        self.K_factor = float(K_factor)
        self.h_gas_corr = float(h_gas_corr)
        self.h_cold_corr = float(h_cold_corr)

        # --- geometry inputs for circuits (sim only) ---
        # Circuits need a back-reference before any design input is evaluated:
        # 'n_channels_all_circuits' is a cross-circuit quantity.
        for circuit in self.cooling_circuits:
            circuit.bind_chamber(self)

        self.build_circuit_x_domain()
        self.build_channel_heights()
        self.build_channel_centerlines()
        self.build_channel_angular_widths()

        # A rounded base input only resolves to full height once the local
        # pitch is known. Build its coolant path before computing
        # length, curvature, or volume. The reference/layout path is unchanged.
        for circuit in self.cooling_circuits:
            if getattr(circuit.cross_section, "height_input", "full") == "base":
                self._build_coolant_centerline(circuit, circuit.channel_full_heights)

        # --- per-circuit preprocessing for solver ---
        for circuit in self.cooling_circuits:
            circuit.finalize()

        # --- hot-gas side (optional/on-demand) ---
        if compute_gas and hasattr(
            self.combustion_transport, "compute_aerothermodynamics"
        ):
            self.combustion_transport.compute_aerothermodynamics(self.contour)

        self.film_cooling = film_cooling
        if self.film_cooling is not None:
            self.film_cooling.x = self._resolve_signed_fraction_to_x(
                self.film_cooling.x_fraction
            )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Domain → centerline → section scalars (sim-only)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def build_circuit_x_domain(self):
        """
        Convert each circuit's fractional span into an x-grid whose size
        scales with the fraction of the overall contour length covered.
        Uses at least 3 nodes per circuit.
        """
        x_min = float(self.contour.xs[0])
        x_max = float(self.contour.xs[-1])
        L_tot = max(1e-30, x_max - x_min)  # guard zero-length contours

        MIN_NODES = 3

        for circuit in self.cooling_circuits:
            f0, f1 = circuit.span

            # Map signed fractional spans to absolute x, keeping your original convention
            x0 = f0 * (x_max if f0 >= 0.0 else -x_min)
            x1 = f1 * (x_max if f1 >= 0.0 else -x_min)

            L_seg = abs(x1 - x0)
            frac = L_seg / L_tot
            n_here = max(MIN_NODES, int(round(self.n_nodes * frac)))

            if x0 <= x1:
                x_domain = np.linspace(x0, x1, n_here)
            else:
                # reversed span: keep coolant marching direction by reversing
                x_domain = np.linspace(x1, x0, n_here)[::-1]

            circuit.set_x_domain(x_domain)

    def build_channel_centerlines(self):
        if not self.cooling_circuits:
            return

        # Use one integration grid for the reference angular laws while
        # retaining each circuit's independent simulation grid. Thus equal
        # placement laws produce the same underlying reference path without
        # changing any transport discretization.
        shared_reference_x = np.unique(
            np.concatenate(
                [
                    np.asarray(circuit.x_domain, dtype=float)
                    for circuit in self.cooling_circuits
                ]
            )
        )

        for circuit in self.cooling_circuits:
            xs = circuit.x_domain

            # The cross-section models use a wall/surface reference, whereas
            # length and curvature must follow the coolant centroid.
            section_radii = np.array(
                [
                    circuit.placement.compute_centerline_radius(x, self.contour)
                    for x in xs
                ],
                dtype=float,
            )
            section_radii += np.asarray(
                circuit.hot_side_layer_thickness(xs),
                dtype=float,
            )
            reference_x = shared_reference_x
            section_dtheta_dx = np.array(
                [
                    circuit.placement.dtheta_dx(x, self.contour, circuit)
                    for x in reference_x
                ],
                dtype=float,
            )

            # The section-reference curve owns the CAD/layout angular path.
            reference_theta = np.zeros_like(reference_x, dtype=float)
            reference_theta[1:] = np.cumsum(
                0.5
                * (section_dtheta_dx[1:] + section_dtheta_dx[:-1])
                * (reference_x[1:] - reference_x[:-1])
            )
            section_theta = np.interp(xs, reference_x, reference_theta)
            self_theta_origin = float(section_theta[0])
            section_theta -= self_theta_origin
            circuit.section_reference_theta_origin_rad = self_theta_origin

            circuit.helix_angle_vals = np.array(
                [
                    circuit.placement.helix_angle(x, self.contour, circuit)
                    for x in xs
                ],
                dtype=float,
            )
            circuit.is_helical = bool(np.any(np.abs(circuit.helix_angle_vals) > 1e-12))

            circuit.set_centerline(
                [np.column_stack([xs, section_radii, section_theta])]
            )
            if getattr(circuit.cross_section, "height_input", "full") != "base":
                self._build_coolant_centerline(circuit, circuit.channel_heights)

    def _build_coolant_centerline(self, circuit, channel_heights):
        """Build the transport path using resolved full channel heights."""
        xs = circuit.x_domain
        wall_thicknesses = np.asarray(
            circuit.total_thickness(xs),
            dtype=float,
        )
        flow_radii = np.array(
            [
                circuit.placement.compute_flow_centerline_radius(
                    x,
                    self.contour,
                    wall_thickness,
                    channel_height,
                )
                for x, wall_thickness, channel_height in zip(
                    xs,
                    wall_thicknesses,
                    channel_heights,
                )
            ],
            dtype=float,
        )
        # Transport length and curvature use a distinct coolant-centroid
        # curve. It honors the requested helix angle at its own radius but
        # never participates in analytical layout validation.
        flow_dr_dx = np.gradient(flow_radii, xs, edge_order=2)
        flow_dtheta_dx = np.array(
            [
                circuit.placement.centerline_dtheta_dx(
                    x,
                    self.contour,
                    flow_radius,
                    dr_dx,
                    circuit,
                )
                for x, flow_radius, dr_dx in zip(
                    xs,
                    flow_radii,
                    flow_dr_dx,
                    strict=True,
                )
            ],
            dtype=float,
        )
        flow_theta = np.zeros_like(xs, dtype=float)
        flow_theta[1:] = np.cumsum(
            0.5 * (flow_dtheta_dx[1:] + flow_dtheta_dx[:-1]) * (xs[1:] - xs[:-1])
        )

        circuit.set_coolant_centerline(
            [np.column_stack([xs, flow_radii, flow_theta])]
        )

    def build_channel_angular_widths(self):
        """
        Compute wedge angle (theta) arrays used by cross-section analytics.

        Priority:
        1) If placement provides channel_angular_width(x), use it.
        2) If placement is 'internal' (non-occluding), use height as an angular-width proxy.
        3) Otherwise, default to an even packing among surface-occluding channels:
           theta(x) = 2π / n_occ(x), where n_occ is provided by the circuit group.
        """
        for circuit in self.cooling_circuits:
            xs = circuit.x_domain
            p = circuit.placement

            if p.has_channel_angular_width:
                angular_widths = np.array(
                    [p.channel_angular_width(x, self.contour, circuit) for x in xs],
                    dtype=float,
                )
                local_sector = angular_widths.copy()

            elif getattr(p, "occludes", True) is False:
                # internal / non-occluding: use height as an angular proxy (sim only)
                angular_widths = np.array(
                    [circuit.channel_height(x) for x in xs],
                    dtype=float,
                )
                local_sector = angular_widths.copy()

            else:
                # uniform angular share among all occluding channels present at x
                n_occ = np.array(
                    [self.number_of_channels(x, occluding_only=True) for x in xs],
                    dtype=float,
                )
                gamma = np.array(
                    [p.helix_angle(x, self.contour, circuit) for x in xs],
                    dtype=float,
                )
                # print
                angular_widths = np.where(
                    n_occ > 0.0,
                    2.0 * np.pi / n_occ,
                    0.0,
                )
                local_sector = np.where(
                    n_occ > 0.0, 2.0 * np.pi * np.cos(gamma) / n_occ, 0.0
                )  # multiplying with cos gamma for helical implementation

            circuit.set_channel_angular_width(angular_widths)
            circuit.set_channel_local_sector(local_sector)

    def build_channel_heights(self):
        """Evaluate the per-circuit height law h(x) on each circuit domain."""
        for circuit in self.cooling_circuits:
            xs = circuit.x_domain
            h = np.array([circuit.channel_height(x) for x in xs], dtype=float)
            circuit.set_channel_height(h)

    @property
    def coolant_volume(self) -> float:
        """Wetted coolant volume of every cooling circuit combined [m³].
